pages.title: A – C
pages.body:
- **Acute angle:** An angle greater than 0° and less than 90°.
- **Adjacent angles:** Angles that share a vertex and a common arm and do not overlap.
- **Algebraic expression:** A combination of numbers, letters (variables) and operation signs, e.g. 3x + 2.
- **Arc:** Part of the circumference of a circle.
- **Back bearing:** The bearing in the opposite direction; it differs from the bearing by 180°.
- **Base (of a power):** The number that is multiplied repeatedly; in 2³ the base is 2.
- **Bearing:** An angle measured clockwise from North, written with three figures.
- **Billion:** One thousand million: 1,000,000,000.
- **Circumference:** The perimeter (distance round) of a circle; C = πd.

pages.title: C – E
pages.body:
- **Co-domain:** The set of outputs of a relation or mapping.
- **Coefficient:** The number multiplying a variable; in 5x the coefficient is 5.
- **Column vector:** A vector written as (x over y), giving its horizontal and vertical components.
- **Complementary angles:** Two angles whose sum is 90°.
- **Congruent:** Exactly the same shape and size.
- **Diameter:** A chord through the centre of a circle; d = 2r.
- **Domain:** The set of inputs of a relation or mapping.
- **Equation:** A statement that two expressions are equal.
- **Equivalent fractions:** Fractions that have the same value, e.g. 1/2 = 2/4.

pages.title: F – P
pages.body:
- **Frequency:** The number of times a value occurs in a set of data.
- **HCF:** Highest Common Factor: the largest number that divides exactly into two or more numbers.
- **Index (exponent):** The small number showing how many times the base is multiplied; in 2³ the index is 3.
- **LCM:** Least Common Multiple: the smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers.
- **Like terms:** Terms with exactly the same variables and powers, e.g. 3ab and −7ab.
- **Mean:** The sum of a set of data divided by the number of items.
- **Median:** The middle value of a set of data arranged in order.
- **Obtuse angle:** An angle greater than 90° and less than 180°.
- **Perimeter:** The total distance round the boundary of a shape.

pages.title: P – R
pages.body:
- **Perpendicular:** At right angles (90°) to a line.
- **Perpendicular bisector:** A line that cuts a segment into two equal parts at right angles.
- **Pi (π):** The ratio of the circumference of any circle to its diameter, approximately 3.142 or 22/7.
- **Place value:** The value of a digit according to its position in a numeral.
- **Prime number:** A whole number with exactly two factors, 1 and itself.
- **Probability:** A measure of how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain).
- **Radius:** A line segment from the centre of a circle to the circle.
- **Rate:** A comparison of two quantities measured in different units, e.g. km per hour.
- **Ratio:** A comparison of two quantities of the same kind, written a : b.

pages.title: R – T
pages.body:
- **Reciprocal:** The number which multiplied by a given number gives 1; the reciprocal of a/b is b/a.
- **Reflection:** A transformation that flips a shape over a mirror line.
- **Reflex angle:** An angle greater than 180° and less than 360°.
- **Sample space:** The set of all possible outcomes of an experiment.
- **Scalar:** A quantity that has magnitude only.
- **Significant figures:** The digits of a number counted from the first non-zero digit.
- **Similar:** Having the same shape (equal angles, proportional sides) but possibly different sizes.
- **Supplementary angles:** Two angles whose sum is 180°.
- **Translation:** A transformation that slides every point of a shape the same distance in the same direction.

pages.title: U – V
pages.body:
- **Unit rate:** A rate for one unit of the second quantity, e.g. GH₵9 per litre.
- **Variable:** A letter or symbol that stands for an unknown number.
- **Vector:** A quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
- **Vertically opposite angles:** Equal angles opposite each other where two straight lines cross.
